title: Matrine Attenuates Neurological Deficits and Neuroinflammation by Inhibiting the HMGB1/RAGE Axis and Ferroptosis in Intracerebral Hemorrhage Mice.
authors: Chen, Pan-Di; Shi, Tao-Tao; Hu, Dan-Yang; Su, Xiao-Na; Jin, Jian-Xiang; Chen, Mao-Song; Wang, Hao; Chen, Wei
journal: The Kaohsiung journal of medical sciences
one_liner_zh: 该文研究苦参碱通过HMGB1/RAGE轴抑制脑出血后神经炎症与铁死亡，仅用分子对接验证小分子-蛋白结合，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a life-threatening stroke subtype that lacks effective drug therapy. In the context of ICH, neuroinflammation, and ferroptosis are key contributors to secondary brain injury. In this study, we assessed the neuroprotective effects of matrine (MAT) and its mechanism of action involving the HMGB1/RAGE axis in an ICH mouse model. ICH was induced in mice by autologous blood injection. MAT (1.5 or 20 mg/kg) was administered orally 5 min postinduction. ICH significantly upregulated RAGE and its associated proteins (HMGB1, protein kinase C [PKC], phospholipase C [PLC], and beta-amyloid), confirming pathway activation. Molecular docking revealed a specific hydrogen bond interaction between MAT and RAGE but not with PKC or PLC. MAT improved neurological performance, reduced hematoma volume and brain edema, and restored blood-brain barrier integrity through upregulation of tight junction proteins (ZO-1, Occludin, Claudin-4). MAT suppressed activation of the HMGB1/RAGE pathway and downstream kinases JNK, p38, ERK1/2, and NF-kappaB p65. It also decreased IL-1beta, IL-6, and TNF-alpha levels, reduced Bax, increased Bcl-2, and mitigated neuronal apoptosis. Additionally, MAT lowered Fe(2+) accumulation, inhibited ACSL4, and restored GPX4 levels, indicating ferroptosis suppression. RAGE knockdown mimicked the effects of MAT and negated its therapeutic benefits. MAT induced no detectable liver or kidney toxicity. This study is the first to demonstrate that MAT alleviates ICH-induced neurological deficits by targeting the HMGB1/RAGE axis-mediated ferroptosis, thereby extending the current understanding of the neuroprotective mechanisms of MAT beyond its known anti-inflammatory and antioxidant actions.
abstract_zh: 脑出血（ICH）是一种危及生命的卒中亚型，目前缺乏有效的药物治疗。在ICH背景下，神经炎症和铁死亡（ferroptosis）是继发性脑损伤的关键因素。在本研究中，我们评估了苦参碱（matrine, MAT）在ICH小鼠模型中的神经保护作用及其涉及HMGB1/RAGE轴的机制。通过自体血注射诱导小鼠ICH。在诱导后5分钟口服给予MAT（1.5或20 mg/kg）。ICH显著上调RAGE及其相关蛋白（HMGB1、蛋白激酶C [PKC]、磷脂酶C [PLC]和β-淀粉样蛋白），证实了通路激活。分子对接（molecular docking）显示MAT与RAGE之间存在特异性氢键相互作用，但与PKC或PLC无此作用。MAT改善了神经功能表现，减少了血肿体积和脑水肿，并通过上调紧密连接蛋白（ZO-1、Occludin、Claudin-4）恢复了血脑屏障完整性。MAT抑制了HMGB1/RAGE通路及下游激酶JNK、p38、ERK1/2和NF-kappaB p65的激活。它还降低了IL-1beta、IL-6和TNF-alpha水平，减少了Bax，增加了Bcl-2，并减轻了神经元凋亡。此外，MAT降低了Fe(2+)积累，抑制了ACSL4，并恢复了GPX4水平，表明其抑制了铁死亡。RAGE敲低模拟了MAT的效果，并抵消了其治疗益处。MAT未诱导可检测的肝或肾毒性。本研究首次证明MAT通过靶向HMGB1/RAGE轴介导的铁死亡来减轻ICH诱导的神经功能缺损，从而将MAT的神经保护机制理解扩展至其已知的抗炎和抗氧化作用之外。
